FAQS

What are corporate actions?

  • • Corporate actions are actions taken by a company that impact the shareholders’ value directly. It is an event that brings material changes to a company and affects its stakeholders.
  • • These may be either monetary e.g. dividend, or non-monetary e.g. Bonus, rights, or stock splits.

What are the types of corporate action?

The different types of corporate actions announced by a company are:
  • •   Rights issue
  • •   Dividend
  • •   Stock Split
  • •   Conversion of debentures into shares
  • •   Amalgamation
  • •   Merger
  • •   Demerger
  • •   Capital reduction / Consolidation of shares
  • •   Buy Back
  • •   Bonus
  • •   Open Offer

Can I check the Corporate Announcements on the Moneycontrol website?

Yes, you can check the details from the Moneycontrol website. Please follow the below mentioned steps:
  • •   Visit https://www.moneycontrol.com/markets/corporate-action/
  • •   Visit a Stock Page, Click on Corporate Action from the Menu.

What is Bonus?

A bonus share is a free share of stock given to current shareholders in a company, based upon the number of shares that the shareholder already owns. While the issue of bonus shares increases the total number of shares issued and owned, it does not change the market capitalization of the company.

What is a dividend?

A dividend can be described as a reward that publicly listed companies extend to their shareholders, and its source is the company’s net profit. Such rewards can either be in the form of cash, cash equivalent, shares, etc. and are mostly paid from the remaining share of profit once essential expenses are met.

What are the types of dividend?

A company may pay a dividend to its shareholders in different forms. Similarly, depending on the frequency of declaration, there are two major types of dividend that shareholders are rewarded with, namely –
  • •   Special Dividend
  • •   Preferred Dividend
  • •   Interim Dividend
  • •   Final Dividend
  • •   Cash
  • •   Assets
  • •   Stocks
  • •   Common Stocks

What is meant by stock split?

A company increases the number of shares that are outstanding by issuing more shares to existing shareholders. For example, in a 2-for-1 stock split, every shareholder holding one share is given an additional share. In such a case, the face value of the share is reduced (say from 10 to 5 per share).

Does Stock Split affect the stock price?

Companies’ stock's price is also affected by a stock split. After a split, the stock price of the company reduces since the number of outstanding shares increases, however the market capitalization remains the same.

What is meant by Rights Issue?

When a company wants to raise capital, issue of fresh shares to the existing shareholders is one option available to the company. In such an issue, existing shareholders have the right to buy a specified number of new shares of the company at a specified price within a specified time. Usually, this price is below the market price. The idea is to reward existing shareholders with an investment opportunity, which is perceived to be attractive.

What is the eligibility of the corporate action?

Let us understand the meaning of different important dates for corporate actions:
  • •   Declaration Date:This is the date on which the board of directors announces to shareholders and the market as a whole that the company will pay a dividend.
  • •   Ex Date: This is the date on which security trades without the benefit of Corporate Action .An investor buying security on or after the ex-date is not eligible for the Corporate Action by the Company.
  • •   Record Date:This is the date on which the company looks at its records to see who are the shareholders of the company entitled for the Corporate Action. An investor holding shares on record date will be eligible for the Corporate Action

Corporate Action News

Carysil: Cautiously optimistic

Highlights Q1 top line grew 13 percent YoY with improvement in margins Quartz sink capacity to touch 90-95 percent in the next two quarters Recently won a global tender for IKEA's non-US quartz sink business Rapidly scaling up presence in the UAE market The stock is close to all-time highs Carysil (CMP: Rs 895; Market Cap: Rs 2,625 crores; Rating: Equal-weight), the sole quartz sink manufacturer in Asia, posted strong Q1 FY26 results with a 13 percent year-on-year (YoY) increase in revenues to Rs 227 crore. Although gross margins came in softer YoY, the company's operating margins improved thanks to better capacity utilisation and reduced freight expenses. While US tariffs pose a challenge, the company is optimistic about volume growth in FY26 due to recent order wins and is targeting a revenue growth of 15-20 percent for the current fiscal year. Quartz sinks driving growth The quarter's performance was mixed across Carysil's product lines. The quartz sinks business, which accounts for ~50 percent of its top line, saw an impressive growth of 23 percent YoY primarily driven by a 22 percent increase in sales volume to 190k units. The capacity utilisation for Quartz sink stood at 75 percent for the quarter. Solid surfaces, the second-largest segment, saw a de-growth of 8 percent due to subdued market demand.  Revenues in the stainless-steel sinks segment also declined 5 percent YoY, despite a 10 percent increase in volumes due to a significant pressure on realisations. Meanwhile, the ‘Kitchen appliances and others’ segment fared exceptionally well, showcasing a 49 percent YoY increase in sales in the quarter gone by. Expanding presence in UAE market United Granite, the US subsidiary, had a slow quarter due to sluggish demand, but its operational performance improved significantly with EBITDA rising to Rs 1.8 crore from Rs 0.4 crore.  Net loss also narrowed to Rs 0.8 crore from Rs 2.2 crore. The management is optimistic about a turnaround in FY26 due to better sourcing and operational efficiencies. The business in the UAE is performing exceptionally well, with appliances accounting for about 80 percent of sales. To capitalise on the margin opportunity, Carysil is planning a major expansion in the GCC, including new showrooms in Dubai (7,000 sq ft) and Muscat (5,000 sq ft). Carysil's UK operations have maintained steady performance despite difficult market conditions. The company anticipates continued positive momentum, supported by new client acquisitions and the benefits of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement. Indian market remains steady Although exports account for majority of its revenue, Carysil continues to build a strong foothold in the Indian market through enhanced brand visibility and a rapidly expanding dealer network. India's Q1 FY26 revenues stood at Rs 40 crore, up 9 percent YoY. Carysil has set a long-term goal of Rs 500 crore in domestic turnover (FY25 revenues: Rs 150 crore), with sinks and faucets as key growth engines. Capacity expansion underway The company has commenced the supply of quartz sinks to Karran USA. Despite higher tariffs, demand in the US has been better than expected, and the company plans to increase its capacity utilisation to 90-95 percent in the next two to three quarters. A 25 percent export tariff is manageable due to the cost and tariff advantages over competitors in Canada, Germany, and Italy. However, a 50 percent tariff would be difficult to pass on, although the overall risk is limited since the US accounts for only 20-25 percent of Carysil's exports. Carysil has also won a major contract from IKEA to supply quartz sinks for its global non-US business. This deal takes its non-US quartz sink market share with IKEA to 75 percent. The company will be investing Rs 20 crore in new moulds, machinery, and infrastructure to meet the incremental demand from IKEA. To address capacity constraints, the company plans to increase its quartz sink production by 25 percent, thereby raising its total capacity to 1.25 million units. Meanwhile, Carysil is undertaking a 70,000-unit expansion of its stainless-steel sink capacity to meet growing demand. This will increase its total capacity to 250,000 units, with the new production lines expected to come online in Q4 FY26. To fund this expansion, Carysil is raising Rs 10 crore through a rights issue, with the total capital expenditure for the project estimated at Rs 30 crore. In addition, Carysil is bidding for a large 500,000-unit order from a major international retailer. Growth trajectory intact Carysil's domestic business is holding steady, though its international segments are showing uneven demand trends between the US and Europe. The earnings growth, however, remains positive due to recent strategic partnerships and announcement. Carysil is in a strong position to benefit from the home improvement industry's shift toward premium offerings because of its favourable cost structure. While Carysil seems to be an interesting growth story, its stock has surged over 60 percent in the past six months. The stock's current price, near its all-time high and trading at 25 times estimated FY27 earnings, seems to have priced in much of the good news. While the long-term outlook is strong, investors should wait for better price points to enter the stock.
